summary: Source decomposition of the statements of the GL_2/Q p-adic local-global compatibility chain, read from the introduction of Emerton's paper: the conjecture itself with its precise local factors and its one likely-false case; Theorem 1.2.1 with its two distinct residual hypotheses and the difference between its embedding and isomorphism cases; the promodularity input and the Fontaine-Mazur and Kisin consequences; the mod p multiplicity theorem and its recovery of Serre's weight and level, answering Serre's own question 3.4(2); and an audit of which of these results carry a Serre-conjecture dependence, which is what the roadmap's R31.6 asks for. The dominant boundary is that only the introduction was read: no proof in this source was inspected, and the p-adic local Langlands correspondence on which everything rests is an unread import that is not in the supplied library. R31.5 is marked not_read.

nodes.title: The completed cohomology of the modular tower and the shape of the local-global conjecture
nodes.statement: Conjecture 1.1.1 of the source: if V is an odd irreducible continuous two-dimensional representation of G_Q over a finite extension E of Q_p, unramified outside a finite set of primes, then the GL_2(A_f)-representation Hom_{E[G_Q]}(V, H-hat^1_E) decomposes as a restricted tensor product B(V|G_{Q_p}) tensor (restricted tensor product over l different from p of pi_l(V)). Here H-hat^1_E is the p-adically completed cohomology of the TOWER OF MODULAR CURVES (defined in the source's 5.1 as the colimit over tame levels K^p of E tensor H-hat^1(K^p)_O, where H-hat^1(K^p)_O is the varpi-adic completion of H^1(K^p)_O = colim over K_p of H^1_et(Y(K_pK^p), O), and (5.1.1)-(5.1.2) identify H-hat^1(K^p)_O / varpi^s with H^1(K^p)_{O/varpi^s}); B(V|G_{Q_p}) is the admissible unitary Banach space representation of GL_2(Q_p) attached to V|G_{Q_p} by the p-adic local Langlands correspondence; and for l different from p, pi_l(V) is the admissible smooth representation of GL_2(Q_l) attached to V|G_{Q_l} by a MODIFIED version of the classical local Langlands correspondence - it coincides with the classical one in the Tate normalization except in those cases where the classical representation is not generic, i.e. not infinite-dimensional. Remark 1.1.2: the conjecture is likely FALSE as stated in one particular case, namely when V|G_{Q_p} is a twist of an extension of the cyclotomic character by the trivial character.
hypotheses: V must be odd, irreducible, continuous, two-dimensional over E, and unramified outside a finite set of primes
H-hat^1_E is the completed cohomology of the modular tower, as constructed in the completed-cohomology roadmap; the conjecture is about the E-coefficient object, not the integral unit ball
the local factor at l different from p is NOT the classical local Langlands representation in general: the modification matters exactly when the classical representation is finite-dimensional
the source itself flags a counterexample case to its own conjecture, so the conjecture is not an available input in that case

It records that at the time the conjecture was first made the p-adic local Langlands correspondence was conjectural, and that it now exists by work of Colmez and Kisin, and that the paper relies heavily on Kisin's deformation-theoretic formulation both to give the conjecture a precise sense and as a tool.

Check the modification of pi_l(V) in a case where the classical local Langlands representation is one-dimensional, confirming it is not the classical one

nodes.title: Theorem 1.2.1: local-global compatibility for promodular V, with the embedding and isomorphism cases
nodes.statement: Let V be a continuous, irreducible, PROMODULAR two-dimensional representation of G_Q over E, unramified outside a finite set of primes, with residual representation V-bar. Assume (a) V-bar is absolutely irreducible (the section opens: V is promodular if it is isomorphic to the Galois representation attached to a cuspidal p-adic modular eigenform of some, possibly non-integral, weight, or equivalently its pseudo-representation lies in the Zariski closure of those attached to classical cuspforms), and (b) V-bar|G_{Q_p} is not isomorphic to chi tensor (upper triangular with diagonal 1, eps) for any k-valued character chi of G_{Q_p}, where eps is the mod p cyclotomic character and the off-diagonal entry may or may not be zero. Then: (1) for some finite set Sigma of primes containing the primes at which V is ramified (page image: V, not V-bar) together with p, there is a NONZERO GL_2(Q_p) x GL_2(A_f^Sigma)-equivariant map B(V|G_{Q_p}) tensor (restricted tensor product over l outside Sigma of pi_l(V)) -> Hom_{E[G_Q]}(V, H-hat^1_E); and if moreover V|G_{Q_p} is neither the direct sum of two characters nor an extension of a character by itself, any such map is an EMBEDDING. (2) If V-bar is p-DISTINGUISHED, i.e. V-bar|G_{Q_p} is not isomorphic to chi tensor (upper triangular with diagonal 1, 1) for any k-valued chi, then there is a GL_2(A_f)-equivariant ISOMORPHISM B(V|G_{Q_p}) tensor (restricted tensor product over all l different from p of pi_l(V)) -> Hom_{E[G_Q]}(V, H-hat^1_E). In the situation of part 2 the source proves a stronger result describing not only the multiplicity spaces but the structure of the summand of H-hat^1_E itself, and even of its unit ball H-hat^1_O, obtained by localizing at V-bar (its Theorem 6.2.13).
hypotheses: V must be PROMODULAR - isomorphic to the Galois representation attached to a cuspidal p-adic modular eigenform of some possibly non-integral weight, equivalently its pseudo-representation lies in the Zariski closure of those attached to classical cuspforms
the two residual hypotheses (a) and (b) are distinct, and part (2) needs the strictly stronger p-distinguished hypothesis
part (1)'s embedding assertion has its OWN extra hypothesis on V (not on V-bar): V|G_{Q_p} neither a direct sum of two characters nor a self-extension
part (1)'s map is equivariant only for GL_2(Q_p) x GL_2(A_f^Sigma), with Sigma a finite set that the theorem does not specify; only part (2) gives full GL_2(A_f)-equivariance
the stronger structural result is about the localization at V-bar of H-hat^1_E and of its unit ball, and uses the local Langlands correspondence IN FAMILIES

nodes.title: Promodularity, and the Fontaine-Mazur and Kisin consequences of the local-global theorem
nodes.statement: Corollary 1.2.2: with V promodular and the same hypotheses (a), (b) as in Theorem 1.2.1: (1) if V|G_{Q_p} is TRIANGULINE then V is a twist of the Galois representation attached to an overconvergent p-adic cuspidal eigenform of finite slope; (2) if V|G_{Q_p} is DE RHAM with distinct Hodge-Tate weights, and V|G_{Q_p} is not the direct sum of two characters with isomorphic reductions mod the uniformizer, then V is a twist of the Galois representation attached to a CLASSICAL cuspidal eigenform of weight k >= 2. Theorem 1.2.3 (attributed to Bockle, Diamond-Flach-Guo, Khare-Wintenberger, Kisin): if V is continuous irreducible odd two-dimensional over E, unramified outside a finite Sigma, and (a) p > 2, (b) V-bar|G_{Q(zeta_p)} is absolutely irreducible, (c) V-bar|G_{Q_p} is not isomorphic to chi tensor (1, *; 0, 1) or chi tensor (1, *; 0, eps) for any k-valued chi, then V is promodular, of tame level divisible only by the primes in Sigma minus {p}. Combining, Theorem 1.2.4 removes the promodularity hypothesis under (a), (b), (c) and yields the Kisin conjecture in the trianguline case and the Fontaine-Mazur conjecture in the de Rham case.
hypotheses: the passage from promodular to unconditional needs p > 2 and the two residual hypotheses of Theorem 1.2.3; the source flags that Kisin's parallel result replaces hypothesis (c) by a different local condition (V-bar|G_{Q_p} not chi tensor (eps, *; 0, 1))

Corollary 1.2.2(2) has an extra hypothesis absent from Theorem 1.2.4(2), namely that V|G_{Q_p} is not a sum of two characters with isomorphic reductions; the source does not say how Theorem 1.2.4 dispenses with it (reviewer observation: such a V has V-bar|G_{Q_p} a twist of the trivial 2-dimensional representation, which hypothesis (c) of Theorem 1.2.3 excludes)

the source attributes its use of Colmez's non-vanishing result for locally algebraic vectors as essential to Corollary 1.2.2, and records that this was a conjectural property of the correspondence at the time the conjecture was formulated
the conclusion is only up to twist

nodes.title: Theorem 1.2.6: the mod p local-global isomorphism, and what it answers
nodes.statement: Let H^1_k denote the inductive limit over all levels N of the etale cohomology with k-coefficients of the full geometrically disconnected modular curve of level N, a representation of G_Q x GL_2(A_f). Theorem 1.2.6, which the source derives as a corollary of the strong form Theorem 6.2.13 of its local-global result: let rho-bar: G_Q -> GL_2(k) be absolutely irreducible and MODULAR (or equivalently, odd, by the now-proved Serre conjecture), suppose p > 2 and that rho-bar|G_{Q_p} is not equivalent to chi tensor (1, *; 0, 1) or chi tensor (1, *; 0, eps) for any k-valued chi. Then there is a k-linear GL_2(A_f)-equivariant isomorphism pi tensor (restricted tensor product over l different from p of pi(rho-bar|G_{Q_l})) -> Hom_{k[G_Q]}(rho-bar, H^1_k), where pi is attached to rho-bar|G_{Q_p} by the mod p local Langlands correspondence and pi(rho-bar|G_{Q_l}) by the mod p local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_l) in families. Remark 1.2.7: the same is EXPECTED but not proved at p = 2, because of imperfect understanding of the mod 2 and 2-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_l), l different from 2. Remark 1.2.8: the theorem generalizes classical mod p multiplicity one results of Mazur, Ribet, Wiles and others, and recovers them by taking invariants under a suitable compact open subgroup - while noting that some of those results are among the tools used in its proof, though only the more straightforward ones, and NOT the existence of companion forms. Remark 1.2.10: the theorem gives a positive answer, for the rho-bar to which it applies, to Serre's question 3.4(2) of whether his conjecture admits a reformulation in terms of the mod p representation theory of the adelic GL_2; from the representation-theoretic statement one recovers the minimal weight (from the socle of pi as a GL_2(Z_p)-representation) and the minimal prime-to-p level (as the conductor of the tensor product away from p).
hypotheses: p > 2 is required; the p = 2 case is expected but not proved, and the obstruction is the local Langlands correspondence at l different from 2, not at 2

the two excluded local shapes at p are the same as in Theorem 1.2.3(c); Remark 1.2.9 records that the first is conjectured to be removable for p > 3 while the second is more problematic because the correct definition of pi is unclear there

the proof uses the more straightforward classical mod p multiplicity one results as tools, but not the existence of companion forms nor [86, Thm 2.1(ii)] in the case where Delta(p) is trivial mod m; the source adds that Theorem 1.2.6 gives a new proof of those results for the rho-bar to which it applies

nodes.title: What in this chain depends on the full Serre conjecture, and what does not
nodes.statement: Audit of the globalisation inputs of the source's results, as the source itself states them: (i) Theorem 1.2.3, which supplies promodularity, is attributed to Bockle, Diamond-Flach-Guo, Khare-Wintenberger and Kisin - i.e. it uses the Serre conjecture machinery, and in particular Khare-Wintenberger. (ii) Theorem 1.2.6's hypothesis is 'absolutely irreducible and modular (or equivalently, odd)', where the equivalence is exactly the Serre conjecture. (iii) Theorem 1.2.1 and Corollary 1.2.2, by contrast, are stated for PROMODULAR V and do not themselves invoke Serre; the Serre-dependence enters only when promodularity is supplied by Theorem 1.2.3. (iv) Theorem 1.2.4 is the combination and therefore inherits (i). Consequence for any argument that claims to reprove Serre's conjecture using these results: it may use Theorem 1.2.1 and Corollary 1.2.2 with an independently established promodularity, but may NOT use Theorem 1.2.3 or the 'equivalently, odd' form of Theorem 1.2.6 without circularity.
hypotheses: this audit records what the SOURCE states about its own inputs; it is not a claim that the dependences are unavoidable
the audit covers only the four numbered results read in the introduction; the body of the paper was not read and may contain further globalisation inputs
promodularity is defined without reference to Serre's conjecture, so it is a hypothesis that can in principle be verified independently
proofSteps: Read off from the statements and attributions in the source's Subsection 1.2.
The distinction between 'promodular' as a hypothesis and 'odd' as a hypothesis is what separates the Serre-free results from the Serre-dependent ones.
acceptance: For each branch of a downstream modularity-lifting argument, check which of Theorems 1.2.1, 1.2.3, 1.2.4, 1.2.6 it uses and whether promodularity is supplied independently

The exclusion recorded in Remark 1.1.2 must be carried through.

Corollary 1.2.2 is deduced from Theorem 1.2.1 together with Colmez's non-vanishing result for locally algebraic vectors; the source says so explicitly ('As explained in [38], Theorem 1.2.1 has the following corollary'). The output supplied is the isomorphism (or embedding) of part (1)/(2), whose locally algebraic vectors are then identified with classical or overconvergent forms.

The audit's content is precisely which of these statements carries a Serre-conjecture dependence; Theorem 1.2.3, which is what upgrades the promodular statements to unconditional ones, is the carrier.

Theorem 1.2.6's hypothesis is stated as 'modular (or equivalently, odd)', with the equivalence citing the Serre-conjecture papers; that is one of the two places where the chain becomes Serre-dependent.

Corrected by the reviewer. CC.2 ('Completion, derived inverse limits and topology') constructs the inverse limits in s, compares the completed module with its finite-coefficient reductions under control hypotheses, and builds the unitary Banach module after inverting p - which is what Emerton's 5.1 uses: H-hat^1(K^p)_O is the varpi-adic completion of H^1(K^p)_O, identified with lim_s H^1(K^p)_{O/varpi^s} by (5.1.1)-(5.1.2), and H-hat^1(K^p)_E is the Banach space with that unit ball. The drafter's claim that H-hat^1 here differs from completed cohomology H-tilde^1 by the Tate-module term of Calegari-Emerton (1.1) was not supported: (5.1.1) makes the two agree at each tame level for the modular tower in degree 1. The colimit over tame levels in H-hat^1_E is an additional step not covered by the survey's fixed-tower objects.
